docs.task: How the review loop counts iterations against its cap, including the YOLO review budget and the review-cap gate.

asks: Explain how the review loop counts iterations against its cap.

data_flow.step: A phase's work pass (implementer, or write-test for the test loop) finishes with status ok. loop_finished sets `LoopNext::Review` when the loop's ReviewMode says to review (Always, or IfCodeChanged and a non-instruction file changed; Never skips review).
The planner spawns the code-reviewer. The `iteration` it puts in `ExecPurpose::Review` is `l.iterations + 1`; that value is a label for the spawn, not what the fold counts.

When the review execution finishes and its submit parses, the fold increments `l.iterations` by one (`l.iterations += 1`). This happens before the BLOCKER check, so a pass that returns BLOCKER or security_block still counts. A review that is interrupted, errors, or has no parseable submit does not increment: interrupted re-runs the step, an error retries once (ERROR_RETRIES) or becomes LoopNext::Failed, and a missing submit becomes LoopNext::Failed. Each WorkLoop (impl_loop and test_loop of a phase) has its own counter.

BLOCKER or security_block: `blocker_open = true`, `LoopNext::Work { kind: WorkKind::BlockerFix }` and return. No cap comparison happens (Hard rule 21), so these passes never open the gate, but they raise `iterations`, which leaves fewer non-BLOCKER passes before the cap.

Otherwise findings split into auto-fixable (apply), HIGH and MEDIUM (remaining), and LOW (leftover_low, never counted against the cap). With auto-fixable findings the loop goes to LoopNext::Autofix first; the AutofixApplied event handler in SessionState::apply later re-adds failed HIGH or MEDIUM autofixes to remaining and calls after_findings. Without auto-fixable findings, after_findings runs immediately.

Empty remaining ends the loop (Stage or Done). Otherwise, if `iterations >= effective_cap(yolo)`, the cap is reached. Below the cap the loop sends the findings to the fix agent (LoopNext::Work Fix) and a completed fix returns to LoopNext::Review.
Non-YOLO at the cap: LoopNext::CapReached. The planner opens GatePayload::ReviewCap with `iterations`, the open findings, and the ledger path. on_gate_opened stores the gate id in `WorkLoop.gate`.

ReviewCap answer `another-pass`: `extra_cap += 1`, then Work Fix with fix_instructions (plus the user's text; when the text is non-empty and the answer was routed it goes through LoopNext::AwaitRoute and the Route-answer judge first). One more fix and one more review follow, so each answer buys exactly one pass; if findings remain, `iterations >= cap + extra_cap` opens a new gate. Any other option: LoopNext::Blocked with the finding count and ledger path, `block_gate_answered = true`.

YOLO at the budget (iterations >= 10 + extra_cap): LoopNext::Resolve, so the planner asks the Resolve-review judge. Judge `fix`: resolve_rounds += 1, open_before_resolve = Some(open count), `extra_cap += 1` (one verification review), then a Fix work pass with per-finding instructions (plain fix_instructions if the list is empty). Judge `block`: LoopNext::Blocked. After the verification review, after_findings runs again: resolve again if the open count fell below open_before_resolve, else Blocked. The conformance fixture yolo_answers_gates_and_extends_review_budget confirms: review #10 -> judge, fix, review #11 (2 -> 1 open) -> judge, fix, review #12 (1 -> 1) -> blocked, with no gate.

If YOLO is toggled on while a loop waits at CapReached, the planner asks the Resolve-review judge instead of opening the gate. If a review_cap gate is already open when YOLO turns on, the YOLO answer plan gives it the fixed choice `another-pass`. The docs say the gate is rarely reached under YOLO for this reason.

PhaseBlocked answer `retry`: `extra_cap = (iterations + REVIEW_CAP) - REVIEW_CAP`, which equals `iterations`. The effective cap becomes iterations plus the mode's base (3 non-YOLO, 10 YOLO), so retry grants a full fresh budget of the current mode. resolve_rounds is reset to 0 and open_before_resolve to None.

patterns.description: WorkLoop::after_findings decides what follows a review whose HIGH and MEDIUM findings remain. It compares iterations with effective_cap(yolo) and sets LoopNext::CapReached (non-YOLO) or LoopNext::Resolve / Blocked (YOLO). The planner only reacts to the resulting LoopNext. The yolo flag is read from SessionState.yolo at the moment the review finishes, so the fold stays a pure function of the event log (YoloSet event).
patterns.name: Cap check lives in the fold, not the planner

patterns.description: The ReviewCap gate follows the repo's gate recipe: payload variant in event.rs with stage() and kind_str() arms, recorded in on_gate_opened (sets WorkLoop.gate), answered in on_gate_answered, opened by the planner, accepted by validate_answer as a Choice, and answered under YOLO by a fixed choice in judge_input::yolo_plan. Options are another-pass (optional text) and anything else, which blocks.
patterns.name: Gate recipe for the review-cap gate

patterns.description: CLAUDE.md pattern 1 and 2: the fold cannot read settings, so facts like auto-fixable rule IDs are recorded in the execution's params (AUTO_FIXABLE_PARAM), and planner-only settings go through PlanCtx (budget_usd, format_commands). Neither mechanism carries a review cap today; REVIEW_CAP and YOLO_REVIEW_BUDGET are constants read directly inside the fold.
patterns.name: Facts from outside the log travel in events or PlanCtx

document.problem: Each work loop (implement or test) keeps a review pass counter and compares it with a cap of 3, or 10 under YOLO, plus an additive extra_cap. Both limits are compile-time constants in state.rs, not settings, and several separate places adjust the cap (another-pass answer, YOLO resolution rounds, phase-blocked retry). The behavior is spread across the fold, the planner, and the YOLO gate plan, so a reader needs one trace of how a pass is counted and what happens at the limit.

Covers the Rust backend fold, planner, judge input, gate payload, tests and docs. document.title: Review loop iteration cap, YOLO review budget, and the review-cap gate

submit.findings_summary: Each WorkLoop (implement and test) has an `iterations` counter that the fold increments in `loop_finished` for every review whose submit parses, including BLOCKER passes. `WorkLoop::after_findings` compares it with `effective_cap(yolo)`, which is `REVIEW_CAP` (3) or `YOLO_REVIEW_BUDGET` (10) plus `extra_cap`, and both constants are compile-time values read inside the fold, not settings or PlanCtx fields. Non-YOLO at the cap yields `LoopNext::CapReached`, which the planner turns into a `GatePayload::ReviewCap` gate. `another-pass` adds 1 to `extra_cap` and anything else blocks the phase. YOLO at the budget goes to the Resolve-review judge: `fix` adds 1 to `extra_cap` and tracks convergence, and non-convergence blocks the phase. `PhaseBlocked` retry sets `extra_cap` to `iterations`. Conformance fixtures and docs pages that cover these are listed in the document.

docs.task: How workspace `limits` settings are defined, validated, and reach the fold or planner.

approaches.best_for: Values the fold itself must use.
approaches.concept: If a new limit changes how an event folds (as a review-pass cap would, because `after_findings` runs inside `apply`), the runner copies the value into an event: either a new field on `SessionOptions` in `SessionCreated`, or a key in the review execution's `params` at spawn.
cons: A value fixed at session creation does not follow later settings changes, unlike the budget.
A `params` key is carried by every review execution and read from the `ExecRecord`; a `SessionOptions` field needs a `#[serde(default)]` for old logs and must stay `Copy`.
Changing `SessionCreated` or `SessionOptions` changes API types and generated TypeScript.
approaches.name: Record the setting in the log, read it in the fold
pros: Keeps the fold a pure function of the log (CLAUDE.md pattern 1).
Direct precedent: `AUTO_FIXABLE_PARAM` is written in `runner.rs` and read in `loop_finished`.
Replays of old logs keep their old behaviour.

approaches.best_for: Spawn-time guards such as the budget.
approaches.concept: Add a field to `PlanCtx`, fill it in `plan_ctx` from `services.workspace().limits`, and apply it in a planner rule. Only works when the decision can be made in `next_steps` rather than in `apply`.
cons: The review cap decision is made in the fold (`after_findings`), so a planner-side check would have to re-derive or override `LoopNext` state, duplicating logic.
The planner output would depend on a fact the log does not record, so a replay with a different setting plans differently (accepted for the budget because it is a spawn guard, not fold state).
approaches.name: Pass the setting through PlanCtx to the planner
pros: Settings are re-read on every planning pass, so a change applies to running sessions.

approaches.best_for: Concurrency and resource limits that the planner and fold do not need.
approaches.concept: Like the slot limiter: the runner reads `services.workspace().limits` when it acts and records nothing.
cons: Cannot affect fold state or planner decisions, so it does not fit a cap on review passes, which is evaluated in the fold.
approaches.name: Read the setting in the runner only

asks: Explain how workspace `limits` settings are defined.
Explain how they reach the fold or the planner.

data_flow.step: The `Limits` struct is part of `WorkspaceSettings` (`#[serde(default)]`, `#[ts(export)]`); defaults are 3 and 25.0, and `seeded()` uses `Limits::default()`.

The user edits the two fields on the Settings General tab. `settingsForm.ts` parses the strings (whole number for parallel, decimal for budget) and reports client-side issues with the same dotted paths.
`POST /api/workspaces/{id}/validate` calls `WorkspaceRt::validate`; `PATCH` calls `save_settings`, which runs `validate` first and writes nothing if any issue remains.

`validate` calls `validate_settings`, which runs sandbox checks, `ostra_core::config::validate_workspace` (limits checks: parallel is at least 1; budget finite and 0 or more), permission rules, and project folder checks.
`write_settings` calls `trust::save_workspace`: `set_access` stores `limits: Some(s.limits.clone())` in the registry; `write_file` removes the `limits` table from `workspace.toml`.

On every read, `ServerServices::workspace()` loads `workspace.toml` and passes it through `trust::effective`, whose `overlay` replaces `s.limits` from the registry (default when the record is absent).
In the driver loop, `drive` calls `plan_ctx(&st)`, which reads `services.workspace().limits.session_budget_usd` and stores `Some(budget)` when greater than 0, then calls `next_steps(&st, &ctx)`.

In the planner's `push`, a `Step::Spawn` is replaced by a `BudgetReached` gate when `spent_usd() >= budget + budget_raised`; `spent_usd` and `budget_raised` come from the fold. The gate answer is folded into `budget_raised` in `on_gate_answered`.
Separately, before each execution starts, `acquire_slot` reads `limits.max_parallel_executions` and waits for a free slot. This value never enters `PlanCtx`, the fold, or the event log.

Review-pass cap, for contrast: `loop_finished` calls `WorkLoop::after_findings(remaining, self.yolo, ledger)`, which compares `iterations` with `effective_cap(yolo)` built from constants. No setting reaches it.

patterns.description: The fold cannot read `project.toml` or settings. The runner writes the project's auto-fixable rule IDs into the review execution's `params` at spawn (the `ExecutionStarted` event), and `loop_finished` reads them back from the `ExecRecord`. This is the existing precedent for any setting-derived value the fold must use.

A new field added inside `Limits` rides along automatically because `Access.limits` stores the whole struct, and `Limits` has `#[serde(default)]` so older records parse with the new field's default.
patterns.name: Registry-only storage of limits (Rule A2)

patterns.description: `WorkLoop::effective_cap` picks `REVIEW_CAP` (3) or `YOLO_REVIEW_BUDGET` (10) from the session's `yolo` flag and adds `extra_cap`. It is called only from `after_findings`, which `loop_finished` and the autofix result path invoke inside `apply`. Neither the planner nor `PlanCtx` is involved; the planner only acts on the resulting `LoopNext::CapReached` / `Resolve` state. The `yolo` flag comes from `SessionCreated.options` or `YoloSet`.
patterns.name: Review cap today: constants inside the fold

document.problem: The workspace `Limits` struct holds two values. Both are read by the engine at run time through `Services::workspace()`: one inside the runner's slot limiter, the other copied into `PlanCtx` and used by a planner guard. The fold (`SessionState::apply`) has no access to settings, so any limit that the fold must apply has to be recorded in an event. The review-pass cap (`REVIEW_CAP`, `YOLO_REVIEW_BUDGET`) is currently a pair of constants applied inside the fold and is not a setting.
document.recommendation: This pass was asked to explain the current mechanism, so no design is required. Where a decision is needed: the fold has no settings input, so a new limit that the fold applies should follow the `AUTO_FIXABLE_PARAM` precedent or ride in `SessionOptions`; a limit that only gates spawns should follow the `PlanCtx.budget_usd` precedent. Because the review cap is evaluated in `WorkLoop::after_findings`, the first approach fits it best. New `Limits` fields need no registry change because `Access.limits` stores the whole struct and `Limits` has `#[serde(default)]`.
document.scope: Task: how workspace `limits` settings are defined, validated, and reach the fold or planner. Covers the two existing limits (`max_parallel_executions`, `session_budget_usd`), their storage, validation, UI, docs, tests, and the way each reaches the runner or planner; also records how the review-pass cap is wired today (constants in the fold) because it is the nearest neighbour that does not use a setting. It does not design a new setting and does not cover the global config.
document.title: Workspace limits settings: definition, validation, and delivery to the fold and planner

submit.findings_summary: `Limits` (max_parallel_executions, session_budget_usd) is defined in ostra-core config.rs and checked in `validate_workspace` during `save_settings`. Both values are stored only in the registry (Rule A2) and overlaid on every read. The engine reaches them through `Services::workspace()`: the budget is copied into `PlanCtx.budget_usd` by `plan_ctx` and applied in a planner guard, and the parallel limit is read directly in `acquire_slot`. The fold has no settings input. The review-pass cap is the constants `REVIEW_CAP` and `YOLO_REVIEW_BUDGET` in `WorkLoop::effective_cap`, called from `after_findings` inside `apply`. A setting-driven cap would need to be recorded in an event, following the `AUTO_FIXABLE_PARAM` or `SessionOptions` precedent. The document lists the web, test, and docs files a new limit would touch.
